short: Two world wars and the collapse of the old imperial order.
full:
The first half of the twentieth century compressed extraordinary change into a few decades. Powered flight, radio, antibiotics, quantum mechanics and relativity all arrived, alongside mass production and mass media.

It was also the most violent period in recorded history. The First World War destroyed four empires and a generation; the unstable settlement that followed, combined with economic collapse, produced fascism and then the Second World War, the Holocaust and the atomic bomb. By 1945 the European empires were exhausted, the United States and Soviet Union stood as superpowers, and the political map of the world was about to be redrawn.
